acceptance.given: The repository-owned pytest terminal selection includes all Package A unit, boundary, negative, and CLI integration cases.

oracle.expected: Terminal execution exposes one independently evaluated expected-result assertion and explicit case/assertion mapping for every executed Package A case.
forbidden: Any executed Package A case lacks an independent expected-result assertion or mapping.
oracle.observable: Pytest output and case/assertion mapping artifacts show an expected-result outcome for every executed Package A case.

acceptance.then: Each selected Package A case completes with its own expected-result assertion.
acceptance.when: When the repository-owned pytest terminal selection completes.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the Package A terminal pytest selection and observe a missing, non-independent, or unmapped expected-result assertion for at least one executed case.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Record and expose an independent expected-result assertion and case/assertion mapping for every executed Package A case.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the declared Package A result and mapping schemas.

slice_hint.state_transition: Package A terminal execution transitions to per-case expected-result evaluation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The terminal selection completes with every executed case independently mapped to an expected-result assertion.

acceptance.given: A Package A negative fixture is selected with rejection declared as its expected outcome.

oracle.expected: The fixture is rejected by validation and pytest reports that rejection assertion as passed.
forbidden: The expected rejection is reported as a suite failure.
The negative fixture is skipped, xfailed, or treated as an unexpected error.
oracle.observable: The negative-fixture test output records expected rejection as a passed assertion.

acceptance.then: The expected rejection is counted as a passing negative test assertion.
acceptance.when: When the selected negative fixture is rejected as expected.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the Package A negative-fixture selector and observe that an expected rejection is not counted as a passed pytest assertion.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Classify an expected rejection from a Package A negative fixture as a passing assertion.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve negative-fixture outcome and pytest reporting semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: Negative-fixture execution transitions from rejection to a passing expected-outcome assertion.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The negative-fixture test passes because validator rejection matches its declared expected outcome.

acceptance.given: A small Package A reference package is integrated into validation under the fixture tree.

oracle.expected: The published CLI consumes the fixture-tree reference package, while no Skill installation or workflow entry is created for it.
forbidden: The reference package is installed as a Skill.
The reference package creates a new workflow entry.
oracle.observable: Validation wiring identifies the fixture-tree package as CLI input and registry inspection finds no corresponding Skill or workflow registration.

acceptance.then: The reference package remains fixture-only and is neither an installed Skill nor a workflow entry.
acceptance.when: When validation wiring and registration surfaces are structurally checked.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Inspect Package A validation wiring and registration surfaces; fail if the reference package is outside the fixture tree or appears in Skill or workflow registration.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Bind the Package A reference package to fixture-only published-CLI validation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No Skill registry or workflow schema changes.

slice_hint.state_transition: Reference-package integration transitions to a verified fixture-only registration boundary.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Structural checks confirm fixture-tree placement and absence from Skill and workflow registrations.

acceptance.given: The Package A validation input is being resolved.

oracle.expected: Resolution selects an existing small Package A reference package under the fixture tree.
forbidden: The reference package is absent from the fixture tree.
A non-Package-A or non-reference package is selected.
oracle.observable: The validator's resolved input identifies an existing fixture-tree Package A reference package.

acceptance.then: The required small Package A reference package is available and selected for validation.
acceptance.when: When the validation input is resolved before terminal execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Resolve the Package A input and fail if the fixture-tree reference package is missing or does not identify as the required Package A reference.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Resolve and validate the required small Package A reference package from the fixture tree.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the Package A validation input contract.

slice_hint.state_transition: Validation input transitions from unresolved to a resolved Package A fixture reference.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Preflight resolution returns an existing fixture-tree Package A reference package.
